Command: Offer a meal offering as prescribed
Summary: The command: Offer a meal offering as prescribed (Leviticus 2:1). The meal offering of fine flour, oil, and frankincense was offered with a memorial portion burned on the altar.
Commandment: Offer a meal offering as prescribed, as prescribed in Leviticus 2:1.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: Fine flour, oil, and frankincense, with a memorial portion burned — a ceremonial law of tribute and thanks. Its goal was to offer the fruit of daily labour to God: the meal offering turned bread-making into worship, the best of the field laid before the LORD. It did not address a particular evil; its work was thanksgiving and dedication, not restraint. The memorial handful burned on the altar said the whole harvest belonged to God, and the offerer gave the first of it back.
